interface_for_harness.entry: ar_trial.run_trial(Harness(wt, driver, run_root, bus_monitor=bool, driver_label=str), fixture, kind, seed, index) -> dict
interface_for_harness.T_definition: T_ms = (caller.t_done_ns - caller.t_spawn_ns)/1e6, harness CLOCK_MONOTONIC; t_spawn_ns immediately before the Driver (bwrap) exec; t_done_ns when the app journal first shows the expected effect with this trial's nonce+pid; verdict also requires journal t_handler_ns >= t_spawn_ns and t_applied_ns <= t_done_ns. Set only when caller.outcome == verified. App startup is before spawn (not in T); fresh verification observation, Driver shutdown and 1 s linger are after done (not in T).
interface_for_harness.paired_design: layout_for(task, seed, variant) is deterministic: give both arms of an AB/BA pair the same seed; use fresh seeds across pairs
interface_for_harness.timed_blocks: pass bus_monitor=False (--no-bus-monitor) or keep it identical across arms; run each timed block via quiet-timed
interface_for_harness.G2_no_unverified_success: ar_oracle.unverified_success_claims (last action claims verified/applied/confirmed but target never changed or changed after the tool returned) is part of every GTK verdict
interface_for_harness.G2_duplicate_mutation: oracle.mutation_count (journal records, one per handler invocation) + extra.do_action_on_bus
interface_for_harness.G2_provenance_matches_route: champion route for every GTK action is 'accessibility' (champion_reference.json routes); stale token has no route (refused)

reference_task.name: gtk3_checkbox:reference
reference_task.app: ar_gtk3_app.py --task checkbox (system /usr/bin/python3 + PyGObject, GTK 3.24); one process per trial

provenance.nonce: 128-bit hex, harness -> app over an inherited pipe (--nonce-fd), read to EOF; never in the UI; the Driver is spawned without it (close_fds) and cannot read the state dir
provenance.ready: app -> harness over a second inherited pipe (--ready-fd): pid, X window id, layout, initial state, CLOCK_MONOTONIC
provenance.journal: <private>/trials/<id>/state/journal.jsonl, written ONLY by the toggle handler (delayed variant: by the GLib timeout the handler schedules); one O_APPEND write per handler invocation with nonce, pid, handler_calls, checked, t_handler_ns, t_applied_ns (host CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
provenance.oracle: ar_oracle.evaluate_gtk, read by the harness outside the sandbox: verified iff exactly one own record, no foreign record, checked == not initial, spawn <= handler <= applied <= done

reference_task.frozen_caller: R2-04 scripted path: list_windows -> get_window_state(tree+screenshot) -> jev-use eligible_controls label lookup -> click(element_token, delivery_mode=background) -> poll journal (0.5 ms, 3 s deadline); no retry, no redispatch, no trace marks, no model
reference_task.driver_sandbox: ar_sandbox.driver_argv: bwrap --ro-bind / / --dev-bind /dev /dev --bind <trial_home> --bind <session XDG_RUNTIME_DIR> --tmpfs <private_root> --remount-ro <private_root> --die-with-parent -- <driver> mcp; HOME/TMPDIR in a fresh per-trial home; no pid/net/time namespace (shared CLOCK_MONOTONIC)

controls.negative_stale_token: observe twice, click the replaced snapshot's token -> must be refused with a stale code, journal empty, 0 DoAction
controls.canary_absent: no control has the target label (tree size kept) -> caller refused/unknown, journal empty
controls.canary_disabled: target eligible at observation; harness tells the app (control socket) to make it insensitive; caller clicks the fresh token -> Driver dispatch reached, outcome refused/unknown, journal empty
controls.delayed_effect: effect applied 200-500 ms (seeded) after the handler -> verified once, done >= applied, observed delay >= 200 ms, 1 caller dispatch, 1 DoAction, no early Driver claim
controls.focus_steal: separate 'User notes' process holds focus; 30-200 ms after the toggle the app maps a 'Notice' toplevel and takes focus (fresh server timestamp) -> verified once, xprop -spy journal shows the steal, focus ends with the user window

spot_checks.gtk3_text:text_save: ar_gtk3_app.py --task text: seeded field + Save labels; caller set_value(unique value) then click Save; oracle = Save-handler journal record note_saved == value, exactly once
spot_checks.browser:fill_submit: jev-use fixture_server PAGE + capture-phase listener journal + seeded padding; caller browser_prepare(isolated_new) -> navigate -> semantic_v2 refs -> browser_type token -> browser_click(foreground) -> poll /state; oracle evaluate_browser: /state.submitted == token, exactly one POST (server CLOCK_MONOTONIC stamp <= done), in-order trusted pointerdown->mousedown->pointerup->mouseup->click on Submit then submit, no untrusted click
spot_checks.browser_selfcheck: Driver-free oracle validation: harness-launched Chrome (sandbox on, throwaway profile) filled+submitted via XTest (must verify) and page-script button.click() (isTrusted false, must NOT verify)

external_checks.process_socket_file_diff: inventories of the private session tree (from the xvfb-run ancestor) before spawn, before Driver shutdown, after exit + 1 s: processes (comm), listening sockets held by them (unix ACC, tcp LISTEN, udp bound), files under trial home / session runtime dir / /dev/shm; harness pids and descendants ignored; normalised (digits, hex, mktemp suffixes); flattened to a signature
external_checks.duplicate_mutation_counter: journal record count + dbus-monitor Action.DoAction count on the private AT-SPI bus
external_checks.oracle_timestamps: app CLOCK_MONOTONIC handler/applied stamps; browser server CLOCK_MONOTONIC receive stamps

validation.evidence_class: REAL (correctness only; no timing claim; not under the quiet-lane lock; nice 10; private sessions under hostless)

champion_observations_worth_knowing: the Driver omits insensitive controls from get_window_state entirely
a click on a control made insensitive after observation still sends DoAction, reports effect unverifiable, and changes nothing
the focus guard restores the first observed change (incl. a stacking_top change from a newly mapped window) and returns; a focus steal after that restore is not undone
the Driver forks pacman at startup (installation detection), does a network version check and default telemetry; all in the reference set
inside hostless every root-owned file is uid 65534, so the isolated browser launch is refused
deviations: browser spot check cannot run on any Driver under hostless (see blockers); its oracle is validated Driver-free
the browser Driver would run without bwrap even when unblocked (same root-ownership check); HOME/TMPDIR still per trial
delayed variant journal line is written by the GLib timeout the handler schedules
focus_steal timing chosen inside the champion's settle window (30-200 ms after the toggle)
canary_disabled disables after observation (champion omits insensitive controls)
Driver HOME/TMPDIR moved to a fresh per-trial home (R2-04 used one session HOME)
bus monitor on during validation; off or identical across arms for timed blocks
n01_packet: not present at writing (artifacts/r2/n-01 empty; w1-n01-native-ab at 28b915ae9); nothing duplicated
blockers: browser:fill_submit spot check is blocked on the champion: hostless (bwrap user namespace) shows root-owned /opt/google/chrome as uid 65534 and the Driver's isolated launch requires a root-owned, non-writable Chromium (platform-linux browser_platform.rs trusted_root_owned_installation) -> browser_route_unavailable 10/10. The only alternative route (existing_profile) needs an explicit grant (safety relaxation), not used. Owner decision needed: an isolation that keeps host uid 0 as root, or accept browser_selfcheck + gtk3_text as the pre-keep spot checks.
near_miss: host-shell python3 heredocs were used for file edits and to read JSON ledgers (no GUI import, no display/session access, no effect possible); all later code execution moved under hostless. All Driver/GTK/Chrome/test runs were under hostless + private session.
